Almanac Victorian Era.Summary: Old Farmer's Almanac, 'Flower Meanings: The Language of Flowers' (Catherine Boeckmann). The chart reflects mainly Victorian flower language; meanings vary by culture and source.
Almanac Victorian Era.Source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Flower Meanings (Victorian-era chart)

Almanac Victorian Era.Summary: Learning flower symbolism became a popular pastime in the 1800s. Nearly all Victorian homes kept guidebooks for deciphering the 'language' alongside the Bible, though definitions shifted depending on the source.
Almanac Victorian Era.Source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Flower Meanings (Victorian-era chart)

Almanac Victorian Era.Summary: Flowers delivered messages that couldn't be spoken aloud. A 'yes' answer came as flowers handed over with the right hand; the left hand meant 'no.'
Almanac Victorian Era.Source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Flower Meanings (Victorian-era chart)

Almanac Victorian Era.Summary: Plants could also express negative feelings: pomegranate for 'conceit,' aloe for 'bitterness.' A yellow carnation returned to a suitor expressed 'disdain.'
Almanac Victorian Era.Source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Flower Meanings (Victorian-era chart)

Almanac Victorian Era.Summary: How flowers were presented changed the message: given upside down, the meaning was reversed. Ribbon tied to the left meant the symbolism applied to the giver; tied to the right, to the recipient. A wilted bouquet delivered an obvious message.
Almanac Victorian Era.Source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Flower Meanings (Victorian-era chart)

Almanac Victorian Era.Summary: Bluebells and kindness, peonies and bashfulness, rosemary and remembrance, tulips and passion.
Almanac Victorian Era.Source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Flower Meanings (Victorian-era chart)

Almanac Victorian Era.Summary: Meanings and traditions have changed over time, and different cultures assign varying ideas to the same species.
Almanac Victorian Era.Source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Flower Meanings (Victorian-era chart)

Almanac Wedding.Detail: One tradition is to select wedding bouquet flowers based on plant symbolism.
Almanac Wedding.Source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Flower Meanings (Victorian-era chart)

Almanac Wedding.Detail: All-white bouquet: lily-of-the-valley (trustworthiness, purity), sweet William (gallantry), hyacinth (loveliness), myrtle (love in marriage), ivy (continuity) — together expressing hope for a loving, everlasting marriage.
Almanac Wedding.Source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Flower Meanings (Victorian-era chart)

Almanac Wedding.Detail: The groom wore a flower from the bridal bouquet in his buttonhole, from the medieval tradition of a man wearing his lady's colors to declare his love.
Almanac Wedding.Source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Flower Meanings (Victorian-era chart)

Almanac Wedding.Detail: Give each bridesmaid a bouquet featuring a signature flower whose meaning suits her personality.
Almanac Wedding.Source: Old Farmer's Almanac - Flower Meanings (Victorian-era chart)
